# Return to Draft - Revisiting Guidance

We have all experienced instances in which Return to Draft (RTD) is the best way forward for a manuscript. As a journal administrator, you may note that there are elements that need to be addressed and resubmitted before the manuscript can pass to an editor for peer review.

If you notice an uptick in occurrences of RTD, please take a moment to investigate possible recurring mistakes and misunderstandings.

Here are some questions to ask yourself and your editors if you are noticing more manuscripts being Returned to Draft:

* Regarding formatting concerns: is it absolutely necessary for references to be formatted before peer review?
  + If Wiley handles production tasks for your journal, including copyediting and typesetting, then you will find that this styling will be done as part of the production process. During copyediting, we follow a two-step process:
    - The first step applies particular styling such as the journal style to references or reference citations in the text, and to other elements of the manuscript.
    - The second step is a language and grammar copyedit to check for spelling errors or grammatical changes that may be needed.
    - If you are unsure of whether you should stop some of these formatting tasks, then please contact the Production Manager for your journal, and they can discuss with you what formatting will be addressed by the production stages, and what changes you can stop making as a result.
  + Around 55% of papers are rejected without going through review. Authors can become frustrated with requests regarding formatting updates, only to be rejected when their paper is seen by an editor. Formatting requests also put strain on the editorial office. Investigating what is necessary to send a paper out for review is imperative in creating a positive author and editorial office experience.
* If Wiley handles production tasks for your journal, including copyediting and typesetting, then you will find that this styling will be done as part of the production process. During copyediting, we follow a two-step process:
* Consider your journal’s author guidelines: do they need to be updated? Perhaps to reflect FreeFormat?
  + With free format submission, authors submit their manuscript in the format of their choice and, upon acceptance for publication, Wiley reformats the manuscript to match the journal's style.
  + Implementing free format is simple and benefits all involved in the process.
* Do custom questions need to be added or adjusted at submission to avoid asking for clarification once a manuscript is received in the editorial office?
  + Do the author guidelines need to be updated to reflect these custom questions?

Taking the time to assess the frequent use of RTD can help to alleviate any additional pressures you face in processing manuscripts for your journal.

To use the Return to Draft option, keep the following in mind.

## In Research Exchange

Use the return to draft option when a manuscript might be suitable for publication, but some elements of the submission need to be addressed and resubmitted before it can pass to an editor for peer review. If chosen, an email will be sent to the author, requesting the changes to be made, and they would need to resubmit the manuscript to an editor in the review module.

When returning a manuscript to draft, it is useful to make references to the guidelines to authors (with a link, if possible).
